data_fields.name: layer0_span_ms
data_fields.donor_constant: 4096 slots x 8 ms = 32768 (computed; layer test uses 1 << 15)

data_fields.name: delay_round_ms
data_fields.donor_constant: round up to multiple of 8; value <= 0 becomes 8

data_fields.name: catchup_turn_cap
data_fields.donor_constant: none in donor; proposed 64 per call

best_idea: A fixed 8 ms wheel with three 4096-slot rings and remainder promotion gives O(1) schedule and cancel for every fight timer, with the due check done once per tick instead of per timer.
decision_why: Fight timers (parry, stagger, leash) last seconds, so one 8 ms ring (32.8 s span) covers them; keep upper layers only if zone grace or respawn timers need hours (row 23). Drop the donor async pool; JS allocation is cheap at this scale.
acceptance: Server test: a 65 ms timer fires on the 72 ms turn; a 3000 ms parry window fires on its own turn, not early; a timer stopped inside an earlier timer's callback in the same turn does not run; after a 10 s stall at most 64 turns run per call and the rest run on later calls.
